headline: Single-cell transcriptomes map cell diversity and regulators in vertebrate tissues
label: Single Cell Transcriptomic Atlases
summary: Single-cell profiling now resolves cell states, trajectories and selection-linked cell contexts across chick, mouse, pig and zebrafish tissues.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell transcriptomics applied to resolve cellular heterogeneity and regulatory programs in developing and adult vertebrate tissues. A single-nucleus study identifies CREM as a brake on myofiber hypertrophy in chickens, while an atlas of about 87,000 cells from the HH17 chick trigeminal ganglion uses RNA velocity to infer trajectories of neural crest- and placode-derived neuroblasts. In mouse, a postnatal day 1 vestibular atlas resolves nine epithelial subpopulations with trajectory topologies and regulons, and primary cortical neuron transcriptomes reveal sex-specific neuropeptide expression. The zebrafish study integrates ATAC- and RNA-seq to separate classical and non-classical osteoblasts and to examine entpd5a regulation. What is new is scEvoSel, which projects population selection statistics (DCMS scores) onto pig muscle and chicken liver single-cell atlases to identify selection-relevant cell contexts.
